title: NY State Assembly · District 77
area: The West Bronx, including Highbridge and surrounding neighborhoods.

context.text: Uncontested race. Incumbent Landon Dais advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed after Shakur Joseph withdrew or was disqualified; no Republican candidate qualified for the general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Landon Dais
candidates.currentRole: NY State Assembly Member, District 77 (since February 2024)

summary.text: Landon Dais is the unopposed Democratic incumbent for Assembly District 77 in the Bronx. An attorney who earlier worked at the Police Athletic League and Turner Construction, he won a February 2024 special election and was elected to a full term in November 2024. He sits on the Banks, Cities, Economic Development, Energy, Housing and Small Business committees, and his campaign website lists affordable housing, street safety, senior services and youth investment among his priorities.

background.text: Born and raised in New York; lives in Highbridge in the Bronx with his wife and two sons, according to his official Assembly biography. He began his education at Fordham Prep.
Earned a B.A. in business management from Morehouse College, an M.S. in real estate development from Columbia University, and a J.D. from Hofstra Law School.
Before law, he served as a Deputy Director at the Police Athletic League and worked at Turner Construction, including on the new Yankee Stadium project.

Worked as an attorney helping small businesses and non-profits; his official biography says his work in the cannabis industry advanced marijuana legalization, workforce development and criminal justice reform. He received the Pro-Bono Attorney of the Year award from Touro College's Jacob D. Fuchsberg Law Center for his work on marijuana arrests, and the NAACP Roy Wilkins Award.

Won the February 2024 special election for Assembly District 77, defeating Republican and Conservative Party candidate Norman McGill, 75.0% to 25.0%; Ballotpedia lists his term as beginning February 14, 2024. He succeeded Latoya Joyner.
Won a full term on November 5, 2024, with 74.3% of the vote (18,104 votes) over Republican Norman McGill and Conservative Party candidate Elianni Del Carmen Tejada Fabian.

Committee assignments for 2025-2026: Banks, Cities, Economic Development/Job Creation/Commerce and Industry, Energy, Housing, and Small Business. He is also a member of the Black Task Force, the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Legislative Caucus and the Puerto Rican/Hispanic Task Force.

Serves on the board of the Mid Bronx Desperadoes (MBD), focusing on affordable housing, and leads the Highbridge Heights Homeowners Association. He coaches baseball in the Foster Park league and founded "Brunch of Dads," a support group for Black and Latino fathers, according to his official biography.

priorities.text: Economic development, investing in youth, access to healthcare, vocational training, and immigration.

positions.summary: Campaign site says access to healthcare is a fundamental right and calls for ensuring all individuals have affordable, comprehensive coverage through healthcare reform.
positions.quote: Access to healthcare is a fundamental right, and we are dedicated to ensuring that all individuals have affordable and comprehensive coverage. This includes addressing issues within Medicare to improve its efficiency and effectiveness, ensuring that our seniors receive the care and support they deserve without financial burden. Through comprehensive healthcare reform, we aim to create a system that prioritizes preventive care, reduces costs, and provides equitable access for all.

positions.summary: Campaign site calls for a mixed approach: legal measures to manage the number of migrants arriving in the state alongside fair and compassionate treatment for migrants already living there, while opposing other states sending migrants to New York.
positions.quote: Immigration in New York State demands a multifaceted approach. This involves advocating for legal measures to manage the influx of migrants while simultaneously devising fair and compassionate strategies for those already residing in the state.

record.text: Assembly committee assignments for 2025-2026: Banks, Cities, Economic Development/Job Creation/Commerce and Industry, Energy, Housing, and Small Business.
Won a February 13, 2024 special election to the Assembly, succeeding Latoya Joyner.

researchNotes: No opposing candidate qualified for the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot in this district. Dais has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; his campaign site's Issues page states specific positions on healthcare and immigration, documented above, but its other listed priority topics (affordable housing, street safety, seniors, vocational training) remain general statements without a stance matching this guide's fixed issue list. Dais's biography relies on his official Assembly page, his campaign site and Ballotpedia; no independent news profile was loaded.
